report:
Fresh final marker followup of meta.book.chapter_names. Preserved prior input/output, started fresh, read the full claim, both implementation entries and all four associated tests, and recaptured BookFixture lines 536–565 and workspace.rs. Compared every fragment by path/selector and both metadata sets. The only delta is an implementation_references association comment in spec.rs. All claim, behavior, tests, helpers, TODO text and metadata are unchanged; no fragments were removed. This isolated marker was assessed against the complete prior findings below.

The ordinary chapter_namespace implementation strips design/, accepts .md/.sage, treats README as its directory, normalizes hyphens to underscores, rejects dotted or invalid ASCII identifier components and joins components with dots. valid_anchor_name enforces ASCII letter/underscore first and ASCII alphanumeric/underscore remainder; qualified combines namespace and local definition. Workspace loading uses SUMMARY destination paths rather than display labels and applies the shared namespace/add_chapter_text path to Markdown and Sage. Headings, titles, sidebar order and source positions do not supply identity. Distinct source paths normalizing to one namespace diagnose collisions; add_chapter_text separately diagnoses duplicate full names, and output URL collisions diagnose distinct namespaces publishing the same page. Rust references resolve exact full inventory keys. The added marker annotates that existing lookup behavior without changing it.

Three ordinary tests provide positive/negative assertions. canonical_inventory_uses_configured_chapters_and_local_names checks exact names meta.authority and meta.call_rules.declared from README/hyphenated Markdown local definitions, the README namespace/context URL and document count. Captured BookFixture/workspace setup uses actual files and configured manual source root. chapter_namespace_collisions_and_duplicate_local_rules_are_errors creates call-rules.md and call_rules.md, requires both namespace and duplicate-full-name diagnostics and rejects an embedded-dot filename and outside-Design path. distinct_namespaces_cannot_publish_the_same_output_url checks README versus index yields the exact output collision diagnostic.

The second implementation entry and fourth test are the explicit TODO names_derive_from_chapter_paths. They retain the broader Markdown/Sage parity and presentation-invariance matrix. Ordinary Markdown qualification/collision assertions do not discharge that TODO. Completing it requires owned Sage fixtures and before/after heading/title/sidebar-order changes with exact unchanged full-name assertions, plus full-name-reference validation and broader invalid ASCII-component cases. The existing comment names format qualification, collisions and display/order invariance; its empty body is not behavioral proof. No N/A entries exist. Current code supports the claim mechanism, while complete behavioral coverage remains visibly deferred.

No source edits, formatting, tests or workspace build were performed in this followup; executed review start/read, capture comparison and record only. The marker-only delta adds no new defect or uncovered behavior. No requested edits.
